title: Setting a fence post in concrete
subtitle: The method for permanent strainer posts that hold under tension.
excerpt: A concrete-set fence post is the correct choice for strainer posts at fence ends, corners, and gateways. Concrete provides lateral support on all sides and prevents the post from levering out under wire tension or gate stress. For intermediate posts, a concrete set is usually unnecessary and adds time and cost without benefit. Here is the method for a concrete-set strainer post.
sourceNotes: NFU, farm fencing guidance. Timber research notes on post setting depths. John Seymour, Self-Sufficient Life (2009).

glossaryTerms.definition: Sloping the top of a concrete collar around a fence post so that rainwater runs away from the post rather than sitting in a collar that could funnel water into the wood and accelerate rot.

content.text: The rule for post depth is one third of the total post length in the ground, plus 15 cm. A 1.8 m post requires a 75 cm hole. For a strainer post handling the tension of three strands of barbed wire, use a post at least 150 mm diameter and set it in concrete over its full hole depth.
Use a post borer (manual or tractor-mounted) to dig a straight-sided hole at least 200 mm in diameter. A round hole holds concrete better than a square hole dug with a spade.
Clear loose soil from the bottom of the hole. The base concrete must rest on firm, undisturbed soil.
Mix a 4:2:1 concrete (4 parts ballast, 2 parts sand, 1 part cement) with enough water to make a stiff but pourable mix. Loose, wet concrete reduces strength.
Pour a 100 mm concrete pad in the base of the hole and tamp it level.
Set the post in the hole, check it is plumb using a spirit level on two adjacent faces, and brace it with two temporary props.
Pour concrete around the post in the hole, pushing it in with a stick to remove air pockets. Fill to 50 mm below the soil surface.
collar at the top of the concrete, sloping it away from the post on all sides. Fill the remaining 50 mm with soil.
Leave the concrete to cure for 48 hours before applying any fence tension. Remove the temporary braces only after the concrete is fully set.

Postcrete (quick-set dry concrete) is poured dry around the post and water is added in the hole. It sets in 10 minutes and can be loaded the same day. Suitable for gate posts and strainer posts on smaller fence runs. Not recommended for posts in waterlogged ground where water control is difficult.
